title: App Mafia: how consumer AI apps hit $50M/yr with influencer marketing and tiny teams
summary: Roundtable with the App Mafia founders on running consumer apps (RizzGPT, UMAX, Cali, Quitter) at roughly $50M combined revenue. Blake's contributions cover launching RizzGPT via underpriced niche creators, the three macro trends behind the app boom, low-maintenance apps with one employee, and how to cold DM a founder.

principles.text: A good app with a working marketing system needs almost no maintenance, so a single hire can run it at high margins.
principles.quote: if you build a good product, you don't have to maintain it. The code continues to provide the service on its own and if you have the marketing system set up correctly, it'll just continue printing.

principles.text: Launch with underpriced, cult-following niche creators; influencer posting alone drove RizzGPT to $80K MRR in three days.
principles.quote: Influencer marketing. Underground niche, underpriced creators, super cult-like following. These these creators posted it and everyone flooded.

principles.text: Wrap a new technology (ChatGPT) into a single-purpose consumer app and market it on social media.
principles.quote: Look at chat GPT. I'm like people should be packaging this into apps.

principles.text: The app boom rests on three trends: LLM functionality, easy building, and dropshipping-style marketing; new winners use at least two.
principles.quote: With Chat GPT and at LLM's you can embed incredible functionality into a single player product.

principles.text: Low-hanging AI ideas are taken, but novel ideas still have room because influencer promos are mostly physical products, not apps.
principles.quote: if you have a novel idea there's still plenty of opportunity on the marketing front

principles.text: Cold DMs work when they lead with credibility or value, not a vague ask for a call.
principles.quote: Zach, although he didn't offer to give me anything, did lead with credibility.
